symbols.name: P
symbols.role: superpopulation law of potential outcome-delay vectors

symbols.name: D
symbols.role: possibly extended calendar delay to revelation

symbols.name: V
symbols.role: calendar revelation time of the assigned response

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: For calendar time \(s\), \(\mathcal F_s\) is generated by assignments through \(\min\{s,T\}\), auxiliary randomization, and every revealed record \((t,W_t,V_t,D_t(W_t),Y_t(W_t))\) with \(t\leq T\) and \(V_t\leq s\)

symbols.name: N
symbols.role: number of assignments to arm \(a\) by time \(s\)

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: \(O_{T,\Delta}\) contains \((W_t,\pi_t)_{t\leq T}\) and every record \((t,W_t,V_t,D_t(W_t),Y_t(W_t))\) with \(t\leq T\) and \(V_t\leq H_T\); thus each terminally revealed assigned outcome is linked to its assignment, calendar revelation time, and observed delay

symbols.name: g
symbols.role: main-prefix guaranteed age at terminal observation

symbols.name: h
symbols.role: old-prefix guaranteed age at terminal observation

symbols.name: vtail
symbols.role: second-moment envelope for the old-tail correction

symbols.name: vhat
symbols.def: the usual sample variance of the \(K_a(n_T)\) variables \(X_{a,j}^{\Delta}\)

assumptions.condition: The vectors \(\{(Y_t(a),D_t(a)):a\in\mathcal A\}\) are independent and identically distributed over \(t\) under \(P\).
For every \(t\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(|Y_t(a)|\leq1\) almost surely.
For every \(t\leq T\), \(P(W_t=a\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},\{Y_t(a'),D_t(a'):a'\in\mathcal A\})=\pi_t(a)\) for each \(a\in\mathcal A\).
For every \(t\leq T\), \(ct^{-\alpha}\leq\pi_t(1)\leq Ct^{-\alpha}\) almost surely.

novel.justification: Deterministically clipped response-adaptive rules with a prespecified decaying exploration schedule satisfy this comparability regime; the constants permit substantial adaptation while keeping the rare-arm information order stable.

assumptions.condition: For every \(t\leq T\), \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\) almost surely.

definitions.name: Informative-delay adaptive experiment class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)=\{(P,\Pi,T):\text{ass:iid-arrivals, ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:polynomial-delay-envelope, ass:sequential-randomization, and ass:rare-arm-envelope hold at index }T\}\).

definitions.name: One-sided forced-exploration comparison class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)=\{(P,\Pi,T):\text{ass:iid-arrivals, ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:polynomial-delay-envelope, ass:sequential-randomization, ass:one-sided-forced-exploration, and ass:control-floor hold at index }T\}\).

definitions.name: Two-cohort schedule
definitions.construction: Choose fixed \(\rho\in(\max\{1/2,(1-\alpha)/(1-\alpha+\beta)\},1)\), set \(m_T=k_T=\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor\), \(n_T=T-m_T\), and, for prespecified \(\Delta_T\geq0\), set \(g_{T,\Delta}=m_T+\Delta_T\) and \(h_{T,\Delta}=T+\Delta_T-k_T\).

definitions.name: Deterministic arm quotas
definitions.construction: Set \(e_1(t)=ct^{-\alpha}\), \(e_0(t)=\varepsilon\), \(Q_a(s)=\sum_{t\leq s}e_a(t)\), and \(K_a(s)=\max\{2,\lfloor Q_a(s)-\sqrt{8Q_a(s)\log T}\rfloor\}\); set \(J_a=K_a(k_T)\) and \(E_T=\bigcap_{a\in\mathcal A}\{N_a(n_T)\geq K_a(n_T),\ N_a(k_T)\geq J_a\}\).

definitions.name: Fixed-quota two-cohort estimator
definitions.construction: Using \(O_{T,\Delta}\), on \(E_T\) index each arm's assignments by tape order. For \(j\leq K_a(n_T)\), set \(X_{a,j}^{\Delta}=Y_{a,j}\mathbf 1\{D_{a,j}\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}\); for \(j\leq J_a\), set \(R_{a,j}^{\Delta}=Y_{a,j}\mathbf 1\{g_{T,\Delta}<D_{a,j}\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\). Each indicator is computed from the recorded revelation time, with an outcome absent by \(H_T\) assigned indicator zero. Set \(M_{a,\Delta}=K_a(n_T)^{-1}\sum_{j\leq K_a(n_T)}X_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), \(U_{a,\Delta}=J_a^{-1}\sum_{j\leq J_a}R_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), and \(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=(M_{1,\Delta}+U_{1,\Delta})-(M_{0,\Delta}+U_{0,\Delta})\). Set \(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=0\) on \(E_T^c\).

definitions.name: Observable main-prefix standard error and gate
definitions.construction: On \(E_T\), let \(\widehat\sigma_{X,a,\Delta}^2\) be the usual sample variance of the \(K_a(n_T)\) main-prefix variables in arm \(a\), set \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}^2=\widehat\sigma_{X,1,\Delta}^2/K_1(n_T)+\widehat\sigma_{X,0,\Delta}^2/K_0(n_T)\), and set \(G_{T,\Delta}=\{\widehat\sigma_{X,1,\Delta}^2+\mathbf 1\{\alpha=0\}\widehat\sigma_{X,0,\Delta}^2\geq2/\log T\}\). On \(E_T^c\), set \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}=0\) and \(G_{T,\Delta}=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Bounded-shift Gaussian critical value
definitions.construction: For \(u\geq0\), \(c_\eta(u)\) is the unique positive solution of \(\Phi(c_\eta(u)-u)+\Phi(c_\eta(u)+u)-1=1-\eta\).

definitions.name: Measurable gate-and-fallback interval
definitions.construction: Let \(x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\), \(S_T=K_1(n_T)^{-1}+K_0(n_T)^{-1}\), \(v_{T,\Delta}=\min\{1,L(1+g_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}\), \(a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}\), and \(A_{a,T,\Delta}(x)=\sqrt{2v_{T,\Delta}x/J_a}+4x/(3J_a)\). Define \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}=[\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\pm\{a_T+A_{1,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+B_{T,\Delta}\}]\cap[-2,2]\). Define \(d_{T,\Delta}=A_{1,T,\Delta}(4\log T)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(4\log T)\) and \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}=[\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\pm\{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})+d_{T,\Delta}\}]\cap[-2,2]\), with \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}=I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) when \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}=0\). Finally, \(I_{T,\Delta}=[-2,2]\) on \(E_T^c\), \(I_{T,\Delta}=I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) on \(E_T\cap G_{T,\Delta}\), and \(I_{T,\Delta}=I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) on \(E_T\cap G_{T,\Delta}^c\).

definitions.name: Ordinary Wald interval
definitions.construction: Let \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}=[\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\pm z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_{T,\Delta}]\cap[-2,2]\), with the same quota-failure convention as \(I_{T,\Delta}\) and with no tail pad.

definitions.name: Modulus handle for exact expected-length optimality
definitions.construction: At \(\Delta_T=0\), use the observed-experiment modulus generated by common-policy likelihood paths and hidden-sign tail perturbations, then optimize worst-case \(\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}\)-length over all \(O_{T,0}\)-measurable uniformly honest intervals for \(\tau\), where the expectation integrates over outcome-delay arrivals under \(P\) and any randomization induced by \(\Pi\), to characterize \(\mathcal C_\eta^*(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\).

statements.statement: For every \((P,\Pi,T)\) in \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the law of \(O_{T,\Delta}\) equals the law obtained from two independent infinite arm tapes with respective marginals \((Y(a),D(a))\), where policy \(\Pi\) consumes the next unused entry of the assigned tape and reveals the record \((t,W_t,V_t,D_t(W_t),Y_t(W_t))\) at calendar time \(V_t\). Consequently, every deterministic prefix of each tape is an independent and identically distributed arm sample, unconditionally and without imposing independence between \(Y(a)\) and \(D(a)\).
statements.justification: This observed-kernel equivalence is the device that converts arbitrary predictable allocation into deterministic independent arm prefixes.
statements.gap: Adaptive AIPW proofs use martingale centering, while reward-dependent-delay lower bounds use tailored instances; neither supplies this unconditional observed-law reduction with delayed histories.
statements.consumer: The reduction permits fixed-quota inference for any logged policy obeying the exploration envelope, including policies whose scaled propensities do not converge.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the deterministic quotas in \(E_T\) satisfy \(P(E_T^c)\leq4T^{-4}\) for all sufficiently large \(T\), and \(K_1(n_T)\asymp T^{1-\alpha}\), \(K_0(n_T)\asymp T\), \(J_1\asymp T^{\rho(1-\alpha)}\), and \(J_0\asymp T^\rho\).
statements.justification: A uniform quota guarantee makes the estimator measurable without conditioning on successful adaptive recruitment.
statements.gap: Existing adaptive-inference proofs generally normalize by random information or assume allocation convergence; the deterministic lower-envelope quota is policy-uniform.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can prespecify sample prefixes and use the full parameter interval on rare quota failures without selective-inference corrections.

statements.statement: On the arm-tape experiment, \(P(M_{a,\Delta}+U_{a,\Delta})=P[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}]\), \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}=2L(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}(1+o(1))\), and \(\operatorname{Var}_P(U_{1,\Delta}-U_{0,\Delta})\leq v_{T,\Delta}(J_1^{-1}+J_0^{-1})=O(T^{-\rho\beta-\rho(1-\alpha)})=o(T^{-(1-\alpha)})\), uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) and deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\).
statements.justification: The shifted old cohort uses every response observable by the prespecified terminal time and leaves only the \(T+\Delta_T\) tail while contributing negligible noise at the rare-arm sampling scale.
statements.gap: Single-age delayed estimators leave bias of order \(m_T^{-\beta}\); no located inference result uses an overlapping old prefix to recover the newly revealed tail under informative delays.
statements.consumer: This correction allows end-of-recruitment inference to use nearly all available follow-up without sacrificing the Gaussian sampling rate.

statements.statement: The interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) is \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable and uniformly honest over \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) without conditioning on \(E_T\) and without convergence of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\). Measurability follows from the recorded calendar revelation times: main-prefix and old-prefix age-window indicators are known at \(H_T\), including when a response remains unrevealed. On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), \(\sup_x|P\{(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta})/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)|\to0\) and \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\) uniformly. If the gate fails, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) retains coverage; if it passes, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\) has the bounded-shift Gaussian coverage envelope, including triangular arrays with variance approaching the threshold \(1/\log T\).
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing uniform studentization result that makes one implementable procedure valid in both Gaussian and degenerate regimes.
statements.gap: Bibaut et al., Hadad et al., and Shi, Wang, and Wu rely on centered scores plus variance consistency or convergence; none treats an outcome-selected reveal process with an overlapping correction and an observable low-variance splice.
statements.consumer: The theorem yields a prespecifiable implementation that does not fail when the inferior-arm outcome variance is small or the adaptive allocation oscillates.

statements.statement: For fixed \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) and any prespecified deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\), there exist constants \(0<c_\eta\leq C_\eta<\infty\) such that \(I_{T,\Delta}\) satisfies \(\inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1)\) and \(\sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}[|I_{T,\Delta}|]\leq C_\eta r_{T,\Delta}\). Conversely, every \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable interval \(J_{T,\Delta}\) with uniform coverage at least \(1-\eta\) satisfies \(\sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}[|J_{T,\Delta}|]\geq c_\eta r_{T,\Delta}\). Here each \(\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}\) integrates over the outcome-delay arrivals under \(P\) and any randomization induced by the predictable adaptive design policy \(\Pi\). The lower bound uses the same fixed admissible policy in each paired experiment, with a prompt-outcome mean tilt for \(T^{-(1-\alpha)/2}\) and hidden-sign laws concentrated at the finite delay \(H_T+1\) for \((1+H_T)^{-\beta}\). At \(\Delta_T=0\), the frontier is \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\).
statements.justification: The two-sided allocation envelope fixes the rare-arm information order: its lower side supports the construction, and its upper side permits a same-policy sampling lower bound, while the delay alternatives certify the hidden-tail term.
statements.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu impose a one-sided forced-exploration lower bound and outcome-delay independence; that regime supports an achievability comparison but does not fix an exact minimax information order or retain an informative hidden-tail shift. Lancewicki et al. prove indistinguishability for regret rather than interval length.
statements.consumer: Investigators can translate a logged exploration schedule and endpoint-tail audit into the shortest defensible order of uncertainty for the eventual treatment contrast.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the deterministic lower-envelope quotas and the interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) remain uniformly honest and have expected length at most a constant multiple of \(r_{T,\Delta}\). This is the achievability reduction under the one-sided polynomial forced-exploration condition used by Shi, Wang, and Wu. No matching \(T^{-(1-\alpha)/2}\) converse is asserted on this enlarged class because policies may allocate the designated arm more often than order \(t^{-\alpha}\).
statements.justification: This separates the one-sided condition needed for a policy-uniform upper bound from the two-sided comparability regime needed to identify an exact minimax sampling frontier.
statements.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu use one-sided forced exploration for delayed asymptotic inference under outcome-delay independence; the proposition isolates what survives under unrestricted outcome-delay dependence without attributing the new two-sided regime to them.
statements.consumer: Analysts whose logs certify only a forced-exploration floor can retain the honest construction while reporting an upper guarantee rather than an exact policy-class minimax rate.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q=(1-\alpha)/2\). Uniformly on \(\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), \(I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\) has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\eta\). For deterministic \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\), there is a Rademacher immediate-outcome plus finite hidden-sign delay family in the same experiment for which \((\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau)/s_{T,0}\Rightarrow N(-u,1)\) and \(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to u>0\); for every fixed \(c'>0\), the limiting coverage of \([\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\) equals \(\Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1\). Hence \(c_\eta(u)\) is attained for symmetric intervals at the phase boundary.
statements.justification: The result converts the phase boundary into an attained local experiment rather than a conservative bias comparison.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár supply the generic bounded-bias Gaussian calibration, while delayed-bandit work does not derive or attain its bias ratio in the adaptive observed experiment.
statements.consumer: This gives trial statisticians the correct critical value when the endpoint-tail and exploration exponents meet at the nonzero-shift boundary.

statements.statement: On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), the ordinary interval \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\), computed from outcomes observed through \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\), is uniformly asymptotically honest if and only if \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\). If this product converges to a positive finite constant, a compatible hidden-sign family has a nonzero shifted-Gaussian limit and ordinary-Wald undercoverage; if it diverges, ordinary-Wald coverage tends to zero along a compatible family. At \(\Delta_T=0\), ordinary Wald is uniformly honest exactly when \(\beta>q\).
statements.justification: Because follow-up changes both truncation ages and the observations entering the statistic, the uniform if-and-only-if criterion separates a class-wide ordinary-Wald guarantee, a class-wide tail-padding requirement, and sufficient endpoint follow-up.
statements.gap: Classical delayed urn inference gives usual asymptotics, and delayed CARA theory assumes ignorable delays; neither characterizes the informative-tail follow-up boundary.
statements.consumer: A protocol can select no pad, a bias-aware pad, or additional follow-up from the prespecified exploration and endpoint-tail exponents.

statements.statement: For a stationary binary-endpoint reanalysis of a logged real-time adaptive trial whose inferior-arm probabilities satisfy the two-sided rare-arm envelope and whose endpoint delays satisfy the polynomial envelope, compute the risk-difference statistic from records observed through \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\). A protocol seeking a uniformly honest guarantee over this informative-delay envelope class may prespecify \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) only when \(T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\); otherwise the protocol requires \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\), \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\), or a prespecified \(\Delta_T\) that makes this ratio vanish. This class-wide necessity does not preclude pointwise validity of ordinary Wald for particular laws, including laws with immediate delays.
statements.justification: This translates the uniform theorem into an auditable protocol-level inference choice for delayed cardiovascular endpoints without imposing a necessity claim on each individual delay law or claiming the original simulations satisfy the assumptions.
statements.gap: Liberali et al. report resampling intervals and inferior-arm precision costs but no uniform coverage theorem under outcome-dependent ascertainment.
statements.consumer: A GUSTO-1 or EUROPA-style protocol can prespecify the tail pad or follow-up period needed for class-wide honesty after verifying the logged propensity and delay-tail envelopes, while permitting an ordinary-Wald pointwise analysis under a separately certified prompt-delay law.

statements.statement: If \(D_t(a)=0\) almost surely for both arms, then for every \(\Delta_T\geq0\), the actual hidden-tail bias satisfies \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\), \(U_{a,\Delta}=0\), and \(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}\) reduces to the difference of independent fixed-quota arm means. On the regular class, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is pointwise asymptotically honest for this prompt-delay law. The generic envelope radius \(B_{T,\Delta}=2\min\{1,L(1+h_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}\) need not equal zero under this specialization; the generic Gaussian branch reduces asymptotically to ordinary Wald only along sequences for which \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\), in which case \(c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})\to z_{1-\eta/2}\).
statements.justification: The reduction separates the zero actual bias of a prompt-delay law from the possibly positive conservative radius retained by the generic envelope-based procedure.
statements.gap: This is a required compatibility check rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementers can use ordinary fixed-quota Wald inference for a certified prompt-delay law and can identify when the generic envelope-based Gaussian branch remains conservatively padded.

statements.statement: At \(\Delta_T=0\), does the normalized minimax expected length \(r_{T,0}^{-1}\inf_{J_T}\sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}[|J_T|]\), where the infimum ranges over all \(O_{T,0}\)-measurable intervals with uniform coverage at least \(1-\eta\) and \(\mathbb E_{P,\Pi}\) integrates over the outcome-delay arrivals under \(P\) and any randomization induced by the predictable adaptive design policy \(\Pi\), converge to \(\mathcal C_\eta^*(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\); and can all asymptotically optimal variable-length intervals be characterized at the Gaussian, bounded-shift, and hidden-tail faces of the observed-experiment modulus?
statements.justification: Order optimality does not determine the economically relevant constant or whether data-dependent length improves on symmetric bias-aware intervals.
statements.gap: Armstrong and Kolesár characterize optimal intervals in Gaussian regression experiments, while no observed adaptive delayed experiment has an exact modulus or variable-length optimum.
statements.consumer: The answer would benchmark the efficiency loss of the measurable two-cohort procedure and determine whether further interval shortening is possible without weakening honesty.

sampling_model.design: Two-arm predictable sequential randomization through recruitment time \(T\), with known logged propensities, deterministic lower-envelope quotas, and records observed through the prespecified terminal time \(H_T=T+\Delta_T\).
sampling_model.units: One independent and identically distributed potential outcome-delay vector arrives at each integer recruitment time \(t\leq T\); each revealed assigned response records its calendar revelation time and realized delay.
sampling_model.treatment: The prespecified rare arm has probability between \(ct^{-\alpha}\) and \(Ct^{-\alpha}\), with \(0<c\leq C\leq1-\varepsilon<1\). In the two-arm simplex, the upper rare-arm envelope implies \(\pi_t(0)\geq1-C\geq\varepsilon\); an explicit control floor is imposed only on the separate one-sided comparison class.
sampling_model.overlap: The novel two-sided polynomial comparability regime fixes the rare-arm information order at \(T^{1-\alpha}\); the one-sided forced-exploration class is retained separately for achievability comparison.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No delay law or outcome regression is estimated. The procedure uses terminally observable fixed-age indicators, sample variances, a known tail envelope, and an observable variance gate.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their estimator converges to a normal distribution under appropriate conditions.
The observed empirical mean is no longer an unbiased estimator of the expected reward.
They only assume that there is a bound on the tail of the delay.
With bounded or sub-Gaussian reward distributions, the upper bounds are optimal with a matching lower bound.
Maximum likelihood estimators from such a trial have the usual asymptotic properties.
The adaptively-weighted estimator is consistent, and the studentized statistic is asymptotically normal.
Their stabilized estimator is asymptotically normal under consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimation.
They derive finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Their central limit theorem enables semiparametrically efficient inference at fixed sample sizes.
They derive the efficient influence function under propensities bounded away from zero and one.

tldr: A two-arm adaptive experiment with a rare arm sampled at a probability comparable to \(t^{-\alpha}\) and an outcome-dependent delay tail bounded by \(L(1+u)^{-\beta}\) admits uniformly honest intervals for the eventual mean contrast with minimax expected length \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\) after prespecified follow-up \(\Delta_T\); at end of recruitment this is \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\). The observed record includes revelation times, so shifted main and old cohort windows are measurable and added follow-up changes the statistic. An observable variance gate splices a bias-aware Gaussian interval to a concentration fallback, and the vanishing tail-envelope-to-standard-error ratio is the boundary for a protocol-level ordinary-Wald guarantee over the full class, although prompt-delay laws can validate ordinary Wald pointwise. Every expected interval length averages over the outcome-delay arrivals and any randomization induced by the predictable adaptive design policy.

project_justification.gap: Delayed adaptive-inference theory centers scores by imposing outcome-delay independence and typically assumes only a forced-exploration floor, whereas reward-dependent-delay theory establishes regret bounds and selection-bias constructions rather than uniformly honest confidence intervals.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved niche is finite-horizon inference for an eventual causal contrast when exploration is two-sided comparable to a vanishing schedule, revelation is informative, the allocation scaling need not converge, and post-recruitment follow-up changes the observed endpoint set.
project_justification.fill: The project combines a revelation-time-complete observed-law arm-tape reduction, deterministic shifted two-cohort prefixes, a uniform variance gate, and same-policy hidden-tail alternatives to deliver the rate frontier, the Wald boundary, and a clinical follow-up rule.

related_work: Shi, Wang, and Wu provide the closest delayed adaptive-inference setup and impose a one-sided polynomial forced-exploration condition; that condition is used here only for the separate achievability reduction, while their formal centering also uses outcome-delay independence. The two-sided comparability condition is a novel design regime: its lower envelope guarantees enough rare-arm observations for the upper construction, whereas its upper envelope prevents the policy class from silently supplying more rare-arm information and is required for the matching same-experiment converse. Hadad et al. and Bibaut et al. supply predictable AIPW weighting and conditional-variance stabilization for prompt outcomes. Manegueu et al. supply the polynomial delay-tail envelope under reward-delay independence. Lancewicki et al. and Tang, Wang, and Zheng show how reward-dependent delays bias observed rewards and construct regret lower bounds; they inform the hidden-tail decomposition rather than serve as interval comparators. Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger establish classical response-adaptive asymptotics with response-dependent delays. Armstrong and Kolesár provide the bounded-bias Gaussian calibration adapted here. Ma, Wang, and Wei derive delayed CARA efficiency under conditional delay-outcome independence and nonvanishing allocation. Liberali et al. provide the cardiovascular-trial consumer and document inferior-arm precision costs in simulations, without a theorem-level coverage guarantee under outcome-dependent ascertainment; the resulting tail-pad or follow-up requirement is therefore a protocol-level condition for uniform validity over the envelope class, not a claim that every individual trial law invalidates ordinary Wald.
technical_internal_limitation: The minimax order has a concentration and two-point route, but the single-procedure claim depends on a uniform studentized approximation at the observable \(1/\log T\) gate. The proof must control the overlap between \(M_{a,\Delta}\) and \(U_{a,\Delta}\), the random sample variance near the gate, and quota-failure conventions without conditioning. The generic radius \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is a class-wide tail envelope rather than the actual bias \(b_{T,\Delta}\); it can remain positive for a prompt-delay law whose actual bias is zero. Exact expected-length constants over randomized or variable-length intervals are not claimed. The model excludes unknown tail envelopes, cross-arrival dependence, and nonstationary endpoint rates; permanent nonrevelation is excluded by the polynomial envelope with \(\beta>0\), not by a separate assumption.
honest_scope: The arm-tape equivalence, quota concentration, shifted old-tail variance calculation, and hidden-sign lower experiment are theorem targets supported by explicit proof routes but remain to be written rigorously. The uniform gate theorem is the principal open proof obligation. The ordinary-Wald boundary is asserted only for uniform honesty of the constructed \(\Delta_T\)-indexed fixed-quota statistic over regular variance subfamilies, not for arbitrary unweighted adaptive estimators or as a necessity statement for every individual law. The two-sided allocation envelope defines the exact frontier class; under the larger one-sided forced-exploration class only achievability is asserted. When delays are identically zero, the actual hidden-tail bias and old-cohort correction vanish and ordinary fixed-quota Wald inference is pointwise valid, while the unchanged generic envelope radius need not vanish numerically. Application to GUSTO-1 or EUROPA requires an external audit of stationarity, logged propensities, the endpoint-tail envelope, and the use of a risk-difference estimand.

seed_details.anchor: ShiWangWu2023DelayedInference, Theorems 4.1--4.3 and Corollary 4.4; LancewickiSegalKorenMansour2021, Section 4 and Theorem 6
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the minimax honest-interval length \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\}\) when delay and outcome may be dependent, using a same-policy likelihood comparison and a revelation-time-measurable two-cohort upper construction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The DAIPW score is no longer conditionally centered because revelation selects outcomes; replace the martingale centering step by an observed-law arm-tape representation and deterministic prefix quotas.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for outcome-dependent delayed adaptive confidence intervals, reward-dependent delayed inference, and two-cohort delayed estimators located regret results and delay-independent inference, but no matching honest-interval phase diagram.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Shi, Wang, and Wu because their Corollary 4.4 already combines polynomial exploration and polynomial delays.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their centering uses outcome-delay independence and therefore deletes the hidden-tail mean shift; their theorem gives no informative-delay lower bound or \(T^{-\beta}\) honest-length term.

seed_details.opportunity: Prove a uniform studentized limit for revelation-time-measurable, follow-up-shifted main and old cohorts, with an observable variance gate and a concentration branch that remains honest when variance collapses.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The conditional-standard-deviation estimator no longer targets a centered score; first remove the predictable stopping clock by fixed arm-tape quotas, then compare the old-cohort correction in \(L_2\) to the main-prefix standard error.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for studentization with informative delayed outcomes and adaptive allocation found conditional-variance stabilization under prompt or independent-delay observation, not a measurable gate spanning Gaussian and degenerate regimes.
seed_details.red_team: A variance gate is a routine splice of a martingale central limit theorem and Bernstein's inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform validity across a random shrinking-variance boundary, with overlapping cohorts and no conditioning on quota success, is precisely where the existing high-level variance-convergence arguments do not apply.

seed_details.opportunity: Characterize uniform ordinary-Wald honesty over the informative-delay envelope class if and only if \(T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\) for the statistic computed through \(T+\Delta_T\), and identify compatible bounded-shift and coverage-collapse sequences otherwise.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The usual Slutsky step must retain, rather than discard, the tail mean as a deterministic local shift and must exhibit a compatible hidden-sign law attaining each boundary shift.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing adaptive cardiovascular trials, outcome-dependent ascertainment, extended follow-up, and Wald coverage found simulation and independent-delay asymptotics but no necessary-and-sufficient frontier for uniform honesty over an informative-delay envelope class.
seed_details.red_team: The condition is immediate from comparing a bias bound with a standard error.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sufficiency is only half the result; necessity requires same-observed-experiment laws and an attained local shifted-Gaussian limit under the adaptive log.

seed_details.anchor: CookMishlerRamdas2024, Section 3 and the betting confidence-sequence theorem; HowardRamdasMcAuliffeSekhon2021, Theorem 1
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a time-uniform confidence sequence with width \(\max\{\sqrt{\log\log t/t^{1-\alpha}},t^{-\beta}\}\) up to necessary stitching factors under informative delays.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The test-supermartingale must be built for revealed, fixed-age scores and then combined with a simultaneous deterministic tail envelope; the pending outcomes themselves are not martingale increments.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for confidence sequences under reward-dependent delays found prompt-outcome adaptive AIPW sequences and generic martingale stitching, but no informative-delay hidden-tail sequence.
seed_details.red_team: Attach \(t^{-\beta}\) to Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas and apply a union bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: A pointwise tail pad is not simultaneous, and cohort ages change with calendar time; optional stopping can select the largest noncentered tail unless a joint construction is proved.

seed_details.anchor: MaWangWei2026CARA, Theorem 1 and Section 6; LiberaliEtAl2025RTAR, Sections 1 and 5
seed_details.opportunity: Choose an exploration floor and post-recruitment follow-up schedule to minimize worst-case interval length plus a patient-welfare cost, with a KKT or saddle-point certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the delay-independent efficient-variance objective by a bias-aware objective containing the adversarial hidden-tail modulus, then optimize jointly over allocation and follow-up.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for optimal adaptive trial design with informative delayed endpoints found forward-looking allocation under conditional delay-outcome independence and simulation-based RTAR, not a certified inference-follow-up optimum.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine scalar optimization once the interval rate is known.
seed_details.rebuttal: The allocation changes both the adaptive information process and the hidden-tail exposure; a valid certificate must optimize over feasible predictable policies rather than over a postulated effective sample size.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive sharp propensity-weighted bounds for the arm contrast when delays may be infinite and informative, with uniform inference for the bound endpoints.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace point identification by an extremal completion of never-revealed outcomes and prove that predictable Horvitz--Thompson empirical distributions recover the observed components.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for adaptive logged assignment paired with informative permanent missingness located generic missing-data bounds and delayed-bandit regret, but no sharp adaptive causal contrast region.
seed_details.red_team: The bounds are Manski's missing-outcome bounds with propensity weights inserted.
seed_details.rebuttal: The closed-form identification endpoints are close to classical bounds, but simultaneous endpoint inference under a history-dependent assignment log is not automatic; the seed is retained only as a lower-tier alternative.

seed_details.opportunity: Characterize a product lower bound between cumulative regret and honest contrast-interval length under reward-dependent delays, matched by forced exploration.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple the regret lower-bound alternative to an inferential two-point alternative while preserving one common informative-delay observation law.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found regret bounds for reward-dependent delays and inference under prompt outcomes, but not their product frontier under a common delayed experiment.
seed_details.red_team: The claimed product is not invariant to the arm gap and the delay law, so a single frontier can be manufactured by parameterization.
seed_details.rebuttal: No canonical normalization survived the scan; without a gap-indexed local parameter space the flagship shape is under-specified.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive a semiparametric efficiency bound for the eventual contrast under informative delays and an attaining adaptive estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The observed-data tangent space must include unrestricted perturbations of the joint outcome-delay law under horizon censoring, so the delay-independent efficient influence function must be reprojected.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair is not occupied, but the polynomial envelope alone yields a nonregular horizon-indexed model whose efficiency bound is not a stable scalar object.
seed_details.red_team: There is no regular semiparametric efficiency problem when the hidden-tail bias is of first order.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds on the full envelope class; a regular efficiency question would require a narrower local model and would no longer settle the named frontier.

seed_details.opportunity: Invert a treatment-label permutation test for the eventual contrast while outcomes arrive under an adaptive policy.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A valid symmetry orbit would have to preserve both the adaptive assignment kernel and the outcome-dependent reveal pattern.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found betting and martingale inversion rather than a treatment-label group action compatible with history-dependent allocation and informative revelation.
seed_details.red_team: Adaptive propensities and informative reveal times destroy the exchangeability required by the proposed permutation orbit.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds without conditioning away the adaptivity, so the seed is rejected rather than rescued by an artificial symmetry assumption.

threads: Shi, Wang, and Wu prove consistency, asymptotic normality, and variance estimation for delayed DAIPW scores and verify a one-sided polynomial forced-exploration lower bound in Corollary 4.4, but their outcome-delay independence centers the reveal-weighted score; they do not impose the novel two-sided comparability regime used for the exact converse here.

Lancewicki, Segal, Koren, and Mansour allow arbitrary reward-delay dependence; Section 4 bounds missing rewards optimistically and pessimistically, and Theorem 6 uses indistinguishable delayed instances for regret rather than honest inference.
Manegueu, Vernade, Carpentier, and Valko impose the polynomial delay-tail envelope in Assumption 1 and derive regret bounds, while explicitly assuming reward-delay independence.

Tang, Wang, and Zheng study strongly reward-dependent delays and matching regret bounds, but their target is cumulative regret and their delay is structurally tied to the reward rather than an adverse polynomial-tail inference class.
literature_map.occupancy: No located result gives the exact informative-delay target-method pair: uniformly honest contrast intervals, predictable vanishing allocation, a matching same-policy lower bound, and the rate \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\).
literature_map.subsumption_check: The closest newer reward-dependent paper, Tang, Wang, and Zheng, does not subsume the kernel because it proves regret guarantees and no confidence-interval coverage or local Gaussian boundary.

threads: Bibaut et al. make consistent conditional-standard-deviation estimation load-bearing in Theorem 1 and Algorithm 1, under prompt outcomes and an exploration lower bound.
Hadad et al. stabilize AIPW variance with predictable weights and prove a studentized martingale limit in Theorem 2, but require centered prompt-outcome scores and high-level variance convergence.

Zhang, Janson, and Murphy develop uniform normal approximation for predictably weighted estimators; this informs the uniformity argument but does not treat noncentered informative revelation or a collapsing-variance splice.
Shi, Wang, and Wu estimate the delayed DAIPW variance in Theorem 4.3, but the proof invokes a centered martingale and an outcome-delay independence condition.
literature_map.occupancy: No located paper proves an observable variance gate with an unconditional fixed-quota fallback for overlapping delayed cohorts without propensity convergence.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Existing martingale studentization results stop before the first changed step because the reveal indicator is outcome-dependent and the correction cohort overlaps the main cohort.

threads: Armstrong and Kolesár characterize bias-aware Gaussian intervals through a worst-case bias-to-standard-error ratio, supplying the calibration but not the delayed experiment.

Bai, Hu, and Rosenberger obtain usual asymptotics for delayed response-adaptive urn trials even when delay depends on treatment and response, under a classical allocation regime rather than polynomially vanishing exploration.
Ma, Wang, and Wei derive delayed CARA efficiency and optimized allocation under conditional delay-outcome independence and propensities bounded away from zero.

Liberali et al. simulate real-time cardiovascular-trial allocation and report wider inferior-arm and odds-ratio intervals, but provide no uniform coverage criterion indexed by delay-tail and exploration exponents.
literature_map.occupancy: No located theorem gives the necessary-and-sufficient criterion \(T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0\) for uniform ordinary-Wald honesty over a class when the statistic's observed age windows shift with follow-up, or its attained bounded-shift boundary.
literature_map.subsumption_check: Classical urn asymptotics and modern delayed-CARA efficiency do not subsume a uniform horizon-censoring result with informative heavy tails and a vanishing inferior-arm allocation.

literature_checklist.author: Bibaut, Dimakopoulou, Kallus, Chambaz, and van der Laan

Lancewicki et al. and Tang, Wang, and Zheng expose reward-dependent delay bias for regret, not uniformly honest inference.","noncollapse_reason":"The novel two-sided allocation regime fixes the rare-arm information order, while the revelation-time-complete observed experiment makes the shifted two-cohort statistic measurable. The nonroutine step is uniform studentization with overlapping cohorts and a shrinking-variance gate.","residual_risk":"The uniform gate theorem is the principal mathematical bottleneck. Exact global minimax constants are deliberately left open.","selected_kernel":"A fixed-quota, follow-up-indexed two-cohort interval for an eventual arm-mean contrast has minimax expected length \\(\\max\\{T^{-(1-\\alpha)/2},(1+T+\\Delta_T)^{-\\beta}\\}\\) under arbitrary outcome-delay dependence, and uniform ordinary-Wald validity over the envelope class is characterized by the tail-envelope-to-standard-error frontier, without excluding pointwise validity for prompt-delay laws.","strict_delta":"The new mathematical object is the joint phase map in \\((\\alpha,\\beta,\\Delta_T)\\), certified by an unconditional arm-tape upper construction on recorded revelation times and same-policy observed-filtration lower experiments; at \\(\\Delta_T=0\\) it yields the headline frontier."}
